analysis.title: Should we fear the upside?
key_insights: Goldman's Codacci-Pisanelli sees a pathway for equities to squeeze higher into year-end despite recent turmoil, after one of the most aggressive deleveraging episodes of the past decade in the GS US prime book left positioning considerably cleaner.
Seasonality is cited as a supportive driver: the final stretch of the year has historically been supportive for equities, and this year's setup follows a violent positioning reset.
S&P 500 buyback demand is estimated at about $5bn per day, with 90% of companies expected to be in their open repurchase window by Monday. Trading volumes picked up in the back half of the week.

Equities absorbed hotter CPI, hawkish Fed commentary, surging yields, an oil rally and negative Nvidia headlines in one week without sustained selling. Goldman reads this as a more supportive market structure, though macro risks remain.

The semiconductor trade has had a sharp reset in positioning and valuations. Goldman says the AI monetization and ROI debate may not resolve until the next earnings cycle, but cleaner positioning leaves room for a squeeze without a better AI narrative.

Nomura says hedging flows from exotic and structured products can force dealers to buy volatility as equities rally and sell volatility as they fall. This produces positive spot-vol correlation, so a rising market does not necessarily mean falling volatility.

sector_views.rationale: Positioning and valuations have reset, which leaves room for a squeeze, but the AI monetization and ROI debate stays unresolved until the next earnings cycle.
